what: Redesign the menu-bar app (macos/) per docs/work/menubar-panel/design.md: no notifications; a last-looked time kept on the daemon's clock; a quiet, new-dot or failed icon; a window-style SwiftUI panel of the newest five unread HIGH items with new ones marked, summaries on hover, row clicks to the #item link, and Open prismis, Refresh and settings in the footer.
why: The design is docs/work/menubar-panel/design.md (gh #105). The shipped app badged 50 of 6,718 unread HIGH items, listed them as a wall of raw titles, and would have sent about 20 banners a day; the operator chose a quiet signal and approved the panel mockup at https://claude.ai/artifact/1Dd1vDXAd1XiaXWitQCBqt.

criteria.given: the macos package after the change
criteria.when: it is built and its tests run
criteria.then: no file under macos/Sources imports UserNotifications or sets a notification delegate, the Poller takes no notifier, and Info.plist declares no notification usage; a poll that finds new items returns a snapshot and posts nothing.

criteria.given: no last-looked file and a real local server listing five unread HIGH items whose newest fetched_at is F
criteria.then: the snapshot holds the five rows with none marked new, the new count is 0, the icon state is quiet, and the last-looked file then holds F.

criteria.given: a last-looked time T and a server whose newest-five listing has two items fetched after T and three before, and whose since=T listing returns those two; the two new items' published_at is older than T
criteria.then: the poll made one request with since=T and one for the newest five (priority=high, unread_only=true, view=list, sort_by=date, limit=5, the key in X-API-Key), the new count is 2, exactly those two rows are marked new, and the icon state is new.

mutations.change: Decide a row's newness from published_at instead of fetched_at; C3 must go red.

criteria.given: the state C3 leaves, on a server whose fetched_at values run an hour ahead of the Mac's clock
criteria.when: the panel-open action runs after the rows are shown, and then another poll runs whose since listing is empty for the stored time
criteria.then: the stored last-looked time equals the newest fetched_at among the rows and new items the panel held, the second poll reports a new count of 0 and the icon state quiet, and the file survives a new store instance reading it.

mutations.change: Store the Mac's current time on panel open instead of the newest fetched_at; C4 must go red.

criteria.given: a poll that succeeded with rows and a new count, then a server answering 500, then 403, then a closed port
criteria.then: each snapshot keeps the last good rows and new count, carries a failure that distinguishes a server error, a refused key and an unreachable daemon, the icon state is failed, and the failure is logged with its reason.

criteria.given: a since listing that returns 100 items, and one that returns 7
criteria.when: the header's count is rendered from each poll
criteria.then: it reads 99+ for the first and 7 for the second.

criteria.given: list-view items with kind vulnerability, a kind the app does not know, no kind, and no summary
criteria.when: they are decoded and given a chip style
criteria.then: every item decodes, missing kind and summary become nil without failing the poll, a known kind gets its own tint, an unknown kind gets the neutral chip, and an item with no kind gets no chip.

criteria.given: base url https://example.test and a row for item 5d937428-3c20-4b87-b342-c7f7a7f615cd
criteria.when: the row's action and the footer's Open prismis action run through the core's opener protocol
criteria.then: the row hands https://example.test/#item=5d937428-3c20-4b87-b342-c7f7a7f615cd to the opener and Open prismis hands https://example.test/.

walks.when: after make install-menubar on the operator's Mac the app is reopened
walks.then: the icon is quiet, and the panel lists the same five items GET /api/entries?priority=high&unread_only=true&view=list&sort_by=date&limit=5 returns from the operator's daemon, laid out as the mockup shows.

walks.when: a HIGH item is fetched on the operator's daemon after the panel was last opened
walks.then: within one poll the icon shows the dot and the panel marks that item new.

walks.when: the operator opens the panel and the next poll runs with nothing newer fetched

outOfScope.summary: No banners at all: a HIGH item reaches the operator only when they glance at the icon.
The panel shows five items; the rest are one click away in the web view.
The new count stops at 100 per check, shown as 99+.
The panel's look is verified by eye against the mockup, not by a test.

stakes: The icon shows a dot exactly when the daemon reports HIGH unread items fetched after the last time the operator opened the panel, and none on a fresh install's first check.
Opening the panel moves the last-looked time to the newest fetched_at the panel holds, so the next check shows no dot until something fetched later arrives.

The panel lists the newest five unread HIGH items with two-line titles, source, a kind chip when the item has a kind, and age; items fetched since the last look are marked; hovering a row shows its summary; clicking it opens its web detail panel.
The header shows the new count (99+ past 99) and when the app last checked; a failed check shows its reason there, keeps the last rows and dims the icon with an amber mark.
The footer opens the daemon's web view, refreshes now, and holds Launch at Login and Quit.
The last-looked time survives a restart and is written atomically.
